other.en: Needs a transcript and the first two pages of the most recent IRS Form 1040.

summary.en: For Class of 2027 seniors living in the US with a GPA of 2.0 or higher. Awards range from $1,000 to $60,000, with most between $1,000 and $5,000. Selection weighs GPA, work experience, extracurriculars, financial need and community service.

notes.en: Deadline is 11:59 PM CT on Dec 15, 2026. Only the first 30,000 community applications are reviewed. Run by Scholarship America.

summary.en: Quarterly essay contest. Open to legal U.S. residents of an eligible state (Texas is one), age 16 or older, with a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher. You need at least one year (or 18 semester hours) left before your undergraduate graduation; if you are not in college yet, you must start your freshman year by the 2027–28 school year.

notes.en: This is the Q-4 contest: it opened Oct 1 and closes Dec 31, 2026 at 11:59:59 PM CT. The contest chart only covers 2026, so 2027 quarters are unconfirmed.

other.en: Submit a two-minute video or a 250–500-word essay. No GPA, test scores or résumé needed.

summary.en: For ages 16–26 who are on track for a diploma or GED, or enrolled in a two-year, four-year, vocational or trade program. Awards are $5,000, $10,000 or $25,000, renewable up to 3 times. Apply with a two-minute video or a 250–500-word essay; no GPA, test scores or résumé are needed.

notes.en: Open to legal residents of the 50 states or D.C., or dependent children of an active-duty U.S. service member.

other.en: Must be currently enrolled in or have finished a high school or college dual-credit course in computer science or engineering, or opt in to Amazon's assessment instead. Must be authorized to work in the U.S.

summary.en: For U.S. high school seniors with financial need and a cumulative GPA of 2.3 or higher on a 4.0 scale who plan a bachelor's in computer science, computer engineering, data science, information systems, or electrical, automation, mechanical or industrial engineering, or a related field. $10,000 per year, up to $40,000 total.

other.en: High financial need. Citizen, national or legal permanent resident of the U.S., Marshall Islands, FSM or Palau.

summary.en: Open to all undergraduate students at U.S.-accredited colleges, with a focus on students at or below the poverty line and first-generation college students. Requires high financial need. You must be enrolling as an undergraduate (associate or bachelor's) and be a citizen, national or legal permanent resident of the U.S., Marshall Islands, FSM or Palau.

amount_display.en: Varies by scholarship; see the summary

other.en: Optional extra section for the Terry Scholarship and the Miguel A. Loya Engineering Scholarship: two essays (overcoming a challenge, and leadership), for U.S. citizens or permanent residents, due Jan 11, 2027.

summary.en: One application for incoming UTEP students. Submitting it gets you considered for the UTEP Excellence Scholarship (top 25% of junior class; $2,000–$8,000 per year, renewable up to 4 years), the Presidential Scholarship (up to 10 students; full cost of attendance, including on-campus housing), and many endowed scholarships, with automatic matching. You can apply before you are admitted: the application tells you to finish your UTEP admission while you wait for results.

notes.en: Submitting lets UTEP share your name, major, address, GPA, FAFSA information (including federal tax information) and email with scholarship donors.

summary.en: One portal, but each fund is its own application. Funds seen so far: Makios Technology Fund (computer/technology majors), El Paso Electric, El Paso Military Officers Association memorial, El Paso in Austin, Catherine L. McPike, Joe and Halina Kallaby/SEAot Leadership Award, and Fabens High School. Each fund's Preview PDF shows its eligibility without applying.

notes.en: Deadline is Feb 15, 2027, 11:59 PM CST, as shown in the logged-in portal. The public page (epcf.org) still says Jan 1–May 1 with no year; trust the portal.

name: FirstLight Community Foundation Graduating Seniors Scholarship

summary.en: Scholarship for graduating seniors from the FirstLight Community Foundation. Expected to open in January 2027.
